newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures looked set to remain rangebound on Wednesday as traders said they were reluctant to make big bets ahead of the outcome of a U.S. monetary policy council meeting.
Although the vast majority of analysts and traders expected the U.S. Federal Reserve to leave interest rates unchanged, and the Bundesbank to follow suit on Thursday, caution prevailed.

The March bond future was ramped up to 130.94 early in the day, largely on the back of talk eminating from German banks that a German industrial production report would be weak, traders in Paris said.

However hopes for a test of the contract high at 131.16 were dashed when the production report came in far stronger than expected. The contract clung onto its gains initially but eventually drifted to a good zone of support above Monday's close where it remained for the rest of the session.
Some traders said even though there were optimistic on the whole, they did not think the futures contract would be able to hurdle 130.94, the high for the day, without some extra favourable news.
"I'm still bullish but the market lacks a general direction," a trader at a French brokerage said.
Others were less upbeat about the scope for further gains at the long end of the French curve.

"The markets are optimistic about the markets but I'm not. When you get 10-year yields at 5.50 (percent) in France investors should think that's probably the bottom," Eric Chaney, economist at Morgan Stanley in Paris said.

He said while there were no signs of a rapid acceleration of growth in Europe, the business cycle was nevertheless picking up in both France and Germany. "It's not quick growth but the point is the trough has past. If the dollar stays around 1.60 (per mark) the markets will realise that rates may not be cut."
A futures trader at a large French bank said Thursday's OAT auction may weigh on bond prices during Wednesday and Thursday.
The Treasury announced earlier on Tuesday it would be selling 23 to 25 billion francs of the new benchmark April 2007 OAT and the April 2011 OAT on Thursday.

Analysts said the size of the auction was relatively high compared with the end of 1996 but that the Treasury would be trying to raise as much money as possible while conditions were favourable to fund a swathe of redemptions later in the year.
Traders said PIBOR contracts were hit early on by some non-resident selling, which was reversed when the franc crept past 3.38 against the mark.

March reached a high of 96.69, up five basis points on the day, before the German production report poured cold water on rate cut hopes, prompting another round of selling. Both March and June contracts settled unchanged.
